title: PREFETCHX: Cross-Core Cache-Agnostic Prefetcher-based Side-Channel Attacks
problem: Modern Intel processors contain an undocumented XPT prefetcher shared across cores that speculatively issues loads bypassing LLC lookups, creating exploitable cross-core side-channel and covert-channel vectors.
motivation: Discovering and mitigating new microarchitectural vulnerabilities in widely-deployed processors is critical for protecting sensitive cryptographic operations and user data.
method: PREFETCHX exploits the shared XPT prefetcher which predicts LLC misses and issues speculative loads to bypass normal cache lookups. The attack measures timing variations caused by prefetcher activity across cores to extract sensitive information including RSA private keys, keystroke patterns, and network traffic, while also implementing covert-channel attacks with low error rates.
key_novelty: Discovery and exploitation of a previously undocumented cross-core shared XPT prefetcher as a cache-agnostic microarchitectural side-channel vector that evades traditional cache-based defenses.
contributions: Identification and characterization of the XPT prefetcher as a cross-core shared microarchitectural resource
Demonstration of PREFETCHX extracting RSA private keys from real-world cryptographic implementations
Side-channel attacks monitoring user keystrokes and network traffic patterns
Covert-channel attacks achieving 122KiB/s capacity with low error rates
limitations: Specific quantitative error rates and broader system-level mitigation strategies are not discussed in the abstract.
